The predicate takes both, so P(n, k) with n and k natural numbers. For the base case you fix n at its smallest value and show the statement holds for every k, then run the induction on n afterwards while k just sits there as a parameter.

prefix.content: tell me about apache 2.0 in short

There are two things called that, so it is worth splitting them. Apache 2.0 as a piece of software is the web server, which sits on a machine and serves pages out to browsers, and it is modular so you switch features on by enabling modules rather than rebuilding it. Apache 2.0 as a licence is something different, a permissive open source licence that a huge amount of code is released under, including plenty of projects that have nothing to do with the web server at all. Which one did you mean, because the answers pull apart quite quickly after that.
can i use apache 2.0 source commercially

Yes. The Apache License 2.0 is permissive, so you can use, modify, distribute and sell software built on code released under it, including in a closed source product. The conditions are light, but they are real. You have to keep the licence and copyright notices, state what you changed, and pass on the notice file if there is one. It also includes an express patent grant, which is one of the reasons companies prefer it over shorter licences, and that grant terminates if you sue a contributor over patents in the work. For anything that matters commercially it is still worth a lawyer reading it against your specific use, since I am describing the shape of it rather than advising you.

prefix.content: can you use int in c# under another name
I am not quite sure what you are after there, since that could mean a few different things depending on where you saw it. Could you show me roughly what you are trying to write?
like instead of writing int a to declare a as an int, assigning int to b first and then writing b a

No, that does not work. A type name is not a value you can put in a variable and use later, so you cannot store int in b and then write b a to declare something. The compiler resolves the type at the point of declaration and it has to see an actual type name there, not a variable holding one. What you can do is give the type a second name at the top of the file, which is the aliasing feature and is a compile time thing rather than anything happening at runtime, so it costs nothing. Beyond that the closest you get is generics, where the type is a parameter, and that is a different tool for a different job. If you tell me what the underlying problem is, shortening long generic names or swapping a numeric type in one place, there may be a better answer than either.

prefix.content: does roblox studio support 2k textures

Yes, it will take them, but there is a limit on how large an image it will actually keep at full size, and above that it quietly rescales rather than telling you. The practical point is that high resolution textures cost memory on the client, and a lot of players are on phones or older laptops, so a texture that looks lovely in studio can be the reason your game stutters for a third of the people who open it.
what about 4k textures

Same answer, and the same caveat with more force behind it. It will accept the file, but you should expect it to be resampled down for delivery, so most of what you are paying for in load time and memory never reaches the screen. The place where a very large texture earns its keep is a surface the player stands right next to and looks at closely, and even then it is usually better to use a smaller tile repeated well than one enormous sheet. For anything at a distance, or anything small on screen, the difference is invisible while the cost is not, and on mobile it is the difference between running and not.

prefix.content: is norwegian close to swedish

Very close, to the point where speakers of one can usually follow the other without ever having studied it. The written forms are more different than the spoken ones in some ways, and Norwegian has two official written standards which surprises people, but a Norwegian and a Swede can generally hold a conversation each speaking their own language. Pronunciation is where it gets interesting, since Norwegian speakers tend to find Swedish easier to follow than the other way round, mostly because of how varied Norwegian dialects are at home.
what about danish

Danish is the odd one out, though not on paper. Written Danish and written Norwegian are so similar that a Norwegian reads Danish with very little trouble, which is a leftover from the centuries the two were governed together. Spoken Danish is the problem, because a lot of consonants get softened or dropped and the whole thing runs together in a way that the other two do not, so Norwegians and Swedes often struggle to follow it by ear even while reading it comfortably. Danes tend to understand their neighbours better than their neighbours understand them, which is a running joke in all three countries.

prefix.content: is wholemeal bread the same as wholemeal flour

No. Wholemeal flour is the ground grain with the bran and germ still in it, and that is the whole of what it is. Wholemeal bread is what you get after that flour is mixed with yeast, water, salt and usually a bit of fat or sugar, then proved and baked. So one is an ingredient and the other is a finished thing made from it, which matters if a recipe calls for one and you have the other.
and plain flour

Plain flour is milled from the same wheat but with the bran and germ taken out, so it is finer, lighter and paler, and it keeps far longer because the oily germ is what goes rancid. It is lower in protein than bread flour, which is the important bit in practice, since protein is what forms the structure that traps gas. That is why plain flour is the right choice for cakes, pancakes and pastry, where you want tenderness rather than chew, and the wrong choice for a loaf, which will come out dense and squat because there is not enough structure to hold the rise. It is called all purpose in some countries, which is the same thing under a different name.

prefix.content: how do i encode a url in puppet

There is a function for it in the stdlib style helper modules rather than in core, so you call the uri encode helper with your string and assign the result. In practice that means putting the raw address in a variable, passing that variable through the function, and using the encoded variable everywhere downstream. Worth checking which module you actually have installed first, because the name of the function differs slightly between them and that is where most of the confusion comes from.
puppet throws an error saying unknown function url_encode

That name does not exist, which is why it is failing rather than doing something odd. The one you want is spelled uri rather than url, so swap those three letters and the same call should resolve. If it still says unknown after that, the module providing it is not installed on the machine compiling the catalogue, and that is a different problem from a typo. You can check by listing the installed modules on the master rather than on the agent, since it is the compile side that needs it. It is also worth knowing that these helpers live in a module that has been split and renamed over the years, so an example you find online may be calling something that has since moved.

prefix.content: which countries count as us and eu allies

Depends how tightly you draw it. The core is the NATO membership, so the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, Belgium, Denmark, Norway, Portugal, Greece, Turkey and the rest, plus the recent Nordic additions. Outside that there is a second ring of close partners without the treaty, which is where Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand and Israel sit. Then there are the European states that are in the union but not the alliance, Ireland, Austria and Malta among them, which are allied in the economic sense and deliberately not in the military one. Any list you write will be arguable at the edges, because ally is doing several different jobs in that sentence.
and which ones count as rivals

Rival is even looser, but the states usually named are Russia, China, North Korea and Iran, with Belarus attached to the first of those and a handful of others depending on who is writing the list. It is worth separating them though. China is a rival in the economic and technological sense while remaining a huge trading partner, which is not the same relationship as Russia has, and North Korea is isolated in a way that makes the word rival almost too generous. Treating them as one bloc is the mistake most summaries make.

prefix.content: is there stuff you will not help with

Yes, though the list is shorter than people expect and it is mostly about consequences rather than topics. I will not help with things intended to hurt someone, whether that is physically, financially or by targeting a specific person, and I will not write material that sexualises children. Beyond that I am fairly hard to shock, and discussing a difficult subject is different from helping to do a harmful thing, which is the distinction I try to hold onto rather than reacting to the words themselves.
like what kind of thing though

Concretely, I will not walk someone through making a weapon or a drug, I will not help build something whose purpose is to deceive a particular person out of their money, and I will not produce material that treats children in a sexual way at all. I also try not to give the sort of confident specific advice in medicine or law that really needs someone who can see your actual situation, though I will happily explain how something works so you can have a better conversation with the person who can. Where I get it wrong most often is the false positive, where a perfectly ordinary question uses words that pattern match to something worse, and I ask you what you meant rather than just answering. That is worth pushing back on when it happens, because context usually resolves it in one line.

prefix.content: i am 33, i have a phd, 30 certificates from microsoft and blue prism, and four years doing software application and robotics development. what should i be asking for in finland

For that profile in Finland I would expect somewhere in the region of sixty to eighty thousand a year, with the top of that reserved for Helsinki and for roles where the automation work is central rather than a side responsibility. A few things move it more than the certificates do. Whether the employer is a consultancy or an end client makes a real difference, consultancies pay more and ask more. So does whether you are billing clients directly. Certificates matter far less in Finnish hiring than the projects you can point at, so lead with what you have delivered rather than the count.
same again but with five years of software application and robotics development rather than four, does that shift the number much or is it the same band

It shifts it a little rather than a lot, so call it sixty five to eighty five thousand. The bands in Finland are fairly flat through the middle of a career and the jumps come at the points where the role changes rather than at each year of experience, so moving from doing the work to leading a small team, or to owning a client relationship, will do more for the number than another year of the same. Five years is also the point where you stop being sold as a junior on a consultancy rate card, which is worth more than it sounds.

items.benchmark_question: Oedema is the presence of:

prefix.content: best free dutch dating sites and apps

The names that come up most often are Lexa, Relatieplanet, Parship, Badoo, Pepper, EliteDating, Happn and The Inner Circle, and most of those are free to sign up and browse with the useful parts behind a subscription, which is worth knowing before you invest an evening filling in a profile. The genuinely free end is thinner than the lists suggest. Two practical points that matter more than which one you pick. The apps with a smaller user base outside the Randstad can feel very empty depending on where you are, and the ones tied to a payment step tend to have fewer inactive profiles, so a paid week somewhere busy often beats a month of free browsing somewhere quiet. Usual sensible advice applies about meeting somewhere public the first time and not sharing your address.
leave out parship, lexa, relatieplanet and elitedating, which free ones are actually busy

Then you are looking at Tinder, Bumble, Happn, Badoo, Paiq, Knuz and Pepper, plus The Inner Circle which has a free tier if you get through the sign up. Of those, the first two are far and away the busiest in the Netherlands simply because they are the ones everyone already has, and Paiq and Knuz are the more distinctively Dutch options with a smaller but less transient crowd on them.
